recommendation: Do NOT rely on long-context as replacement for external memory or routing. The Factory approach (external index + routing + verification) is complementary and necessary even with 1M context.

whatGoesWhere.inManualRouter: Page pointers, required reading maps, phase-to-file routing
whatGoesWhere.inContextOS: Phase history, agent ledger, decision log, risk register
whatGoesWhere.inLongContext: Active task specification, current code being edited, recent conversation
whatGoesWhere.inMCPMemory: Queryable indexes, cross-session state, evidence paths
whatGoesWhere.neverInContext: Entire Factory manual, all governance files, all verifier scripts

coreFinding: Long-context models (1M+ tokens) do NOT eliminate the need for external memory, routing, or proof-of-read. Context window = attention budget, not comprehension guarantee.

factoryApproach.contextOS: Indexes content externally; Codex queries what it needs
factoryApproach.mcpMemory: Provides query layer; doesn't load everything into context
factoryApproach.proofOfRead: Verifies content was processed; doesn't assume attention = comprehension
factoryApproach.manualRouter: Points Codex to correct pages; doesn't load all pages

whyLongContextIsNotEnough: Attention dilution: more tokens = less attention per token
Needle-in-haystack: finding specific info in 1M tokens is probabilistic
No persistence: context window resets between sessions/compactions
No audit: can't prove Codex actually processed specific content
Cost: filling context with reference material burns token budget
